events.title: A Giant Spider!
events.body: A giant spider has moved into the clubhouse. It is wearing a tiny scarf in club colors.

outcomes.successHeadline: A mascot is born
outcomes.text: The spider becomes the club's famous mascot. Supporters share spider memes, pack the stands, and copy its tiny scarf.
The spider vanishes before its mascot debut. The internet remains unmoved.
The groundskeeper calmly relocates the spider and shares a few useful training tips.

events.title: A Meteor Shard!
events.body: A warm blue stone is humming in the center circle. The groundskeeper insists it was not there yesterday.

choices.label: Put it in the trophy case

outcomes.successHeadline: The queue goes round the block
outcomes.text: The shard becomes a glittering local attraction and fans queue around the block.
It cools into a perfectly ordinary rock. The trophy cabinet looks embarrassed.
A delighted geology department pays promptly and promises not to ask about the scorch mark.

events.title: Mysterious Energy Drink
events.body: A salesman in mirrored glasses offers one unlabelled crate and refuses to blink.

outcomes.successHeadline: The cones got alphabetized
outcomes.text: The squad trains at impossible speed and alphabetizes the cones before cooling down.
It tastes like warm cucumber. Everyone spends the afternoon burping in unison.
The salesman vanishes. One useful cooler remains behind.

events.title: The Abandoned Lab
events.body: A team-building bus takes a wrong turn and stops outside a laboratory marked DEFINITELY EMPTY.

outcomes.successHeadline: The lab pays a grant
outcomes.text: The motion sensors wake up and award the club a research grant for excellent footwork.
The only discovery is a vending machine that accepts coins but gives nothing back.
The driver finds the training camp. Nobody mentions the moving curtains.

events.title: Your Hero Gets a Commercial
events.body: The sponsor wants a hero to advertise cereal by blasting open an indestructible breakfast box.

outcomes.successHeadline: That catchphrase is everywhere
outcomes.text: The box explodes into harmless golden flakes. The catchphrase is on every playground by Monday.
The box survives. The spoon does not. The sponsor still pays the appearance fee.
The hero says 'crunch' with tremendous authority.

events.title: A Player in a Slump
events.body: One player stays behind after training, taking the same tired shot again and again.

outcomes.successHeadline: The cardboard dragon works
outcomes.text: Shooting through a cardboard dragon works. The whole squad demands a turn.
The dragon falls over before the first shot. At least everyone laughs.
A day away from the noise restores some perspective.

events.title: Two Players Feud
events.body: Two lockers are now separated by a line of cones and a handwritten border checkpoint.

choices.label: Enter them in a duet challenge

outcomes.successHeadline: The worst anthem ever written
outcomes.text: Their terrible club anthem wins the room and the border checkpoint comes down.
They argue about the chorus. Bert confiscates the microphone.
They cooperate long enough to move a giant tire and forget the original argument.

events.title: A Kid Asks for a Hero
events.body: A handwritten letter asks whether a club hero can visit the local school and rescue sports day.

choices.label: Let the hero run sports day

outcomes.successHeadline: Losing the race on purpose
outcomes.text: The hero loses the egg-and-spoon race on purpose and wins every heart in the playground.
One enthusiastic demonstration launches the beanbag onto the roof. The children call it brilliant.
The class sends back a team photo and thirty-seven tactical suggestions.

events.title: The Scoreboard Predicts Tomorrow
events.body: At midnight the scoreboard displays a result for a match that has not happened yet.

outcomes.successHeadline: The preparation looks like magic
outcomes.text: Every predicted moment arrives. The club's preparation looks like magic.
The display was tomorrow's maintenance date. The tactical session becomes a useful laugh.
It continues glowing for six seconds, then behaves perfectly forever.

events.title: Four Without Losing
events.body: A regional broadcaster wants two minutes on how a club this small stopped losing.

choices.label: Explain exactly how you did it

outcomes.successHeadline: The whole division took notes
outcomes.text: You give the entire plan away on air. It works anyway, and everyone wants to watch the club that says the quiet part.
Three managers copy the plan by Tuesday. Two of them do it better.

choices.label: Credit the squad and stop talking

outcomes.text: You name all eighteen of them, slowly, until the segment runs out of time.

events.title: Through to the Next Round
events.body: The cup tie is won and the scoreboard operator has left the final score up all week on purpose.

choices.label: Leave the score up until the next round

outcomes.successHeadline: Nobody touched the switch for a week
outcomes.text: Supporters detour past the ground just to look at it. The next opponent arrives and reads it twice.
A storm knocks out the second digit. It now reads a much stranger result.

choices.label: Reset it and get back to the league

outcomes.text: The operator photographs it, then resets it, then photographs it again.

events.title: A Thousand Voices
events.body: The turnstile counter passes a thousand and the man who operates it insists on a photograph with it.

choices.label: Open the far side of the ground

outcomes.successHeadline: The far side sings back
outcomes.text: The far terrace fills, learns its own songs by half time, and starts answering the main stand.
Eleven people spread themselves across four hundred seats and enjoy the room.
The photograph goes in the programme. He buys forty copies for relatives.

events.title: A Rival Bids
events.body: A club two divisions up has put a real number on one of your players and given you eight days to think about it.

choices.label: Tell them he is not for sale

outcomes.successHeadline: The answer travels faster than the bid
outcomes.text: Your flat refusal reaches the dressing room before it reaches their chairman. He decides you meant it about all of them.
Their scout keeps turning up anyway, now with a folding chair.

choices.label: Ask to hear the whole offer

outcomes.text: The number is better than you feared and the deadline is real. Bert writes both on the back of a teamsheet.

events.title: Deadline Day
events.body: The rival's final offer expires at five. Their chairman has phoned three times and left the same message.

outcomes.successHeadline: Five o'clock came and went
outcomes.text: Five o'clock passes in total silence. He stays, signs nothing, and plays like a man who was wanted and chose here.
The offer expires and so does his good mood. He asks, politely, to be told next time.
The money lands the same afternoon. The squad understands the arithmetic and hates it politely.

events.title: Two Clubs, One Signature
events.body: The winger you have watched all month is sitting in a cafe with a rival's scout and a second, untouched coffee.

outcomes.successHeadline: The second coffee was yours
outcomes.text: You take the second chair, match the offer to the pound, and he signs a napkin before the rival returns from the counter.
He thanks you both, chooses neither, and moves to a club by the sea.
Your scout spends the afternoon on someone cheaper and, he insists, better.

events.title: A Club Legend Walks In
events.body: A man who played four hundred games here in the seventies is standing in reception holding his own boots.

choices.label: Ask him to take a session

outcomes.successHeadline: One drill, forty years old, still works
outcomes.text: He runs one drill he has sworn by since 1974. It is baffling, exhausting, and by Friday the squad asks for it again.
He mostly tells stories. Excellent stories, and a warm afternoon for everyone.

choices.label: Put the boots in the cabinet

outcomes.text: The boots go on the middle shelf. He visits every other Saturday to check on them.

events.title: The Kid Who Never Misses
events.body: The youth coach has waited outside your office for an hour to tell you about one player and one number.

choices.label: Put him in with the first team

outcomes.successHeadline: The number was not a typo
outcomes.text: He does it again in front of everyone, twice, and the senior squad quietly starts staying behind to watch.
He is nineteen and it shows for ninety minutes. He learns more in that hour than in a month.

choices.label: Leave him where he is winning

outcomes.text: The youth coach is delighted, which is rare, and hands over a session plan built around him.

events.title: The West Stand Leaks
events.body: Four rows of the west stand are now officially a water feature. The safety officer has used the word CLOSED.

choices.label: Patch it with whoever turns up

outcomes.successHeadline: Nine supporters and one long ladder
outcomes.text: Nine supporters, one ladder, and a Sunday. The roof holds, and everyone who helped now owns a small piece of the ground.
The patch survives one shower. A professional is called, and charges for the diagnosis too.
It costs what it costs and is finished by Friday, dry and entirely unremarkable.

events.title: The West Stand Reopens
events.body: The dry rows go back on sale and the supporters who fixed them want the first four seats.

choices.label: Name the rows after the ladder crew

outcomes.successHeadline: Four seats with nine names on them
outcomes.text: Nine names go on a brass strip along four seats. Every one of them brings somebody new the following week.
The engraver misspells two names. Both men decide they prefer the new versions.

choices.label: Just put them back on sale

outcomes.text: They sell out in a morning, mostly to people who now check the roof out of habit.

events.title: A Choir on the Terrace
events.body: Six supporters have started singing in something close to harmony and are asking for a microphone.

outcomes.successHeadline: Six voices, then sixty
outcomes.text: Six voices become sixty by half time. The terrace has a sound now, and it is genuinely quite good.
They attempt a key nobody can reach. The attempt itself becomes the joke of the season.
They sing anyway, all afternoon, and are hoarse and happy by full time.

events.title: The Anthem Gets a Verse
events.body: The terrace choir has written a second verse. It is about the club's plumbing and it is four minutes long.

outcomes.successHeadline: Four minutes about a boiler, charting locally
outcomes.text: The full version is released unedited and charts locally. The boiler becomes the most famous appliance in the county.
Four minutes proves to be three minutes too many. The chorus survives; the verse does not.
The trimmed chorus is sung on the way out of every home game from then on.

events.title: The Postman Says He Is Faster
events.body: The postman has told the whole street he is quicker than your quickest player. Your quickest player has heard.

outcomes.successHeadline: The postman is beaten by a street
outcomes.text: Four hundred people watch a professional footballer beat a postman, and cheer anyway.
He pulls up at forty metres, in front of everybody, holding his hamstring.
A stopwatch, an empty pitch, no audience. The numbers improve quietly.

events.title: Ten Off The Bar
events.body: He wants to stay until he has hit the crossbar ten times. It is already dark.

outcomes.successHeadline: The tenth one goes in off the underside
outcomes.text: Nine hundred shots later the tenth rings off the bar and he finally goes home.
Somewhere after the six hundredth his technique deserts him entirely.
Ten minutes, four attempts, one clean strike to finish on.

events.title: The Rondo Nobody Escapes
events.body: The squad has invented a rondo where one player never gets out of the middle. He has been in there since Tuesday.

choices.label: Leave him in there all week

outcomes.successHeadline: He starts reading the pass before it leaves the foot
outcomes.text: By Friday he is intercepting passes the passer has not decided to make yet.
By Friday he has stopped chasing it at all.
Everybody takes a turn in the middle and the drill works as designed.

events.title: Mark The Hero All Week
events.body: Your defender has asked to spend the week marking the club's own hero in training. The hero finds this funny.

outcomes.successHeadline: By Thursday the hero asks him to stop
outcomes.text: The hero spends four days going nowhere and asks, on Thursday, whether he can mark somebody else.
Four days of being turned inside out in front of everyone.
Half an hour is enough to learn something and not enough to be humiliated.

events.title: The Futsal League Is A Player Short
events.body: The Tuesday futsal league needs one more. The hall is small, the floor is concrete, the tackles are not.

choices.label: Sign him up for the whole run

outcomes.successHeadline: He comes back with a first touch that did not exist in August
outcomes.text: Six weeks in a hall the size of a car park and his first touch is unrecognisable.
Concrete, a bad landing, and a physio who has opinions about futsal.
One game, no scores kept, and a touch that is noticeably tidier by Thursday.

events.title: He Has Asked, In Writing
events.body: He has asked to train twice a day. In writing. With a schedule attached, and a second schedule for the first schedule.

outcomes.successHeadline: He finishes the week fitter than anyone at the club
outcomes.text: Ten sessions in five days, and on Saturday he is still running when everyone else has stopped.
He trains himself into the treatment room by Wednesday afternoon.
One session, done properly, and a night's sleep at the end of it.

events.title: Forty Penalties, Right Now
events.body: The squad has decided your keeper should face forty penalties. Your keeper has decided he agrees.

outcomes.successHeadline: He saves the last one and lies down on the goal line
outcomes.text: By the thirtieth he has stopped diving early and started reading hips.
By the thirtieth he has stopped reading anything and started guessing.
Ten penalties, three saved, and everyone goes in before it gets silly.

events.title: His First Club Wants Him Back
events.body: The club that had him at eleven is holding a testimonial on Sunday. They would like him to play the whole ninety.

outcomes.successHeadline: He gets a standing ovation from four hundred people
outcomes.text: Four hundred people who watched him grow up stand up when he comes off.
Twenty minutes in, on a pitch nobody has repaired since 1994, he limps off.
The shirt is framed behind the bar by Monday lunchtime.

events.title: He Misses A Specific Bakery
events.body: A young player misses home. Not vaguely — he misses his mother, his dog, and one particular bakery by name.

choices.label: Move the family near the ground

outcomes.successHeadline: His mother is at every home game by October
outcomes.text: The club pays the deposit. By October his mother has a seat she considers hers.
They come, they hate it, and they are gone again by the second month. The deposit does not come back.
Two days at home and a box of something from the bakery on the way back.

events.title: His Agent Wants A Number
events.body: His agent wants a number. He wants something else: to know he will play.

outcomes.successHeadline: He signs before the agent finishes his coffee
outcomes.text: You say it plainly and he signs before his agent has finished the coffee.
He repeats the promise to a local reporter, word for word, on the record.
You tell him what you honestly think, which is more than most managers offer.

events.title: A Full Day With The Cameras
events.body: A regional show wants a full day with your most watchable player. They have already written the title card.

outcomes.successHeadline: The segment runs twice and the shop sells out of his number
outcomes.text: It runs twice in one weekend and the shop sells out of his number by Sunday.
The edit finds every dropped pass and none of the good ones.
Twenty minutes, two good answers, and everyone is home by four.

events.title: One Place Left In The Hills
events.body: A recovery camp up in the hills has one place left this week. It is not cheap and the food is famously terrible.

outcomes.successHeadline: He comes back down looking like a different athlete
outcomes.text: Six days of thin air and terrible food, and he comes back down transformed.
Altitude, bad sleep, worse food, and legs heavier than when he left.
A quiet week, no travel, and legs that feel like his own again.

events.title: Six Tuesdays For A Certificate
events.body: A coaching course runs Tuesdays for six weeks. Tuesday is a training day. The course does not care.

choices.label: Send him properly, miss the Tuesdays

outcomes.successHeadline: He comes back running sessions nobody here has seen
outcomes.text: Six Tuesdays gone and he returns with sessions nobody at this level has run before.
Six Tuesdays gone, one laminated certificate, no visible difference.
He does the evenings, keeps his Tuesdays, and picks up two useful things.

events.title: A Fortnight Two Divisions Up
events.body: A club two divisions above will let one of your staff shadow them for a fortnight. They have offered a camp bed.

outcomes.successHeadline: He comes home with a fortnight of somebody else's ideas
outcomes.text: Fourteen days of watching a better club work, and he brings all of it back.
He returns with a system that needs eleven players this club does not have.

choices.label: Ask for their session notes instead

outcomes.text: They send eleven pages. Four of them are usable here.

events.title: Give Me The Week
events.body: Your assistant has asked for one week running everything. Not a session. The whole week.

outcomes.successHeadline: His weeks are worth more than they were on Monday
outcomes.text: Five days, his plan, and the squad arrives on Saturday sharper than it left.
By Wednesday it is clear the week had no plan in it at all.
One session, his own plan, and it goes perfectly well.

events.title: He Wants The Lights Off
events.body: He wants to give the team talk in the dark. He has explained why twice and it has not helped.

outcomes.successHeadline: Nobody says a word for a full minute afterwards
outcomes.text: Eleven grown men sit in the dark and afterwards nobody speaks for a full minute.
Eleven grown men sit in the dark and cannot look at each other for a week.
He speaks well. The lights stay on. Everyone is slightly relieved.

events.title: He Used To Keep Goal
events.body: Your keeper works alone. One of your staff kept goal until his knees stopped him, and has said so out loud.

outcomes.successHeadline: He is a goalkeeping coach now, and the gloves came back out
outcomes.text: Three weeks of courses and the gloves come back out of the loft for good.
It turns out he remembers a great deal less than he told everybody.
An hour on Thursdays, which is an hour more than the keeper had.

events.title: Two Drills, One Week
events.body: Head and assistant have designed the same drill differently and neither will move. Back one of them.

choices.label: Run the one you backed, all week

outcomes.successHeadline: His drill is on the board on Monday and stays there
outcomes.text: You back one in front of the other, and by Friday nobody is arguing.
It does not work, and everybody watched it not work, all week.
Half a week each, no argument settled, no harm done.

events.title: Twelve Seasons And The Boiler
events.body: Twelve seasons of session notes went up with the boiler on Sunday night. He is being very calm about it.

outcomes.successHeadline: The rebuilt folder is better than the one that burned
outcomes.text: A month of evenings, and the new folder is sharper than the one that burned.
Half of what he writes down turns out to be invention.

choices.label: Print what the club has on file

outcomes.text: The club had four seasons backed up. He takes what he can get.

events.title: A Man With A Laptop
events.body: A man with a laptop can measure eleven things nobody here has asked about. He is very confident about all eleven.

outcomes.successHeadline: One of the eleven numbers turns out to matter enormously
outcomes.text: Ten of the numbers mean nothing. The eleventh changes how the week is built.
Eleven numbers, none of which ever mean anything. He keeps the deposit.
Two weeks free, one useful chart, no invoice.

events.title: The Groundskeeper Has His Own Mix
events.body: The groundskeeper has a grass mix of his own and a small regional award he believes justifies it.

outcomes.successHeadline: By September it is the best surface in the division
outcomes.text: By September visiting managers are asking what is in it. He will not say.
It comes up in patches by October and the patches spread.

choices.label: Buy the mix the league recommends

outcomes.text: The league's mix goes down. It is fine. It is extremely fine.

events.title: Forty Supporters And One Weekend
events.body: Forty supporters have offered a weekend, a great deal of enthusiasm, and no qualifications whatsoever.

choices.label: Hand them the keys for the weekend

outcomes.successHeadline: They finish on Sunday night and nobody wants to leave
outcomes.text: Forty people, two days, and on Sunday night nobody wants to go home.
It is charming, it is heartfelt, and a great deal of it is wrong.
They buy the materials, a real firm does the work, everyone is happy.

events.title: A Crate From A Club That Went Up
events.body: A crate arrives from a club that has gone up. Nobody here can name half of what is in it.

outcomes.successHeadline: The machine nobody could name turns out to be the good one
outcomes.text: The machine nobody could name turns out to be the one everybody queues for.
Two machines nobody can use, permanently in the way.
The recognisable half goes in. The rest goes in the loft.

events.title: Blackout Blinds, No Screens After Ten
events.body: The physio wants to change how the dorm works rather than what is in it. Blackout blinds. No screens after ten.

choices.label: Let her rebuild the whole night

outcomes.successHeadline: They wake up on Saturday like a different squad
outcomes.text: Blinds, no screens, a fixed lights-out, and a squad that wakes up different.
Nobody sleeps properly for a fortnight and everybody blames the blinds.
The blinds go up. Nobody notices for a fortnight, then everybody does.

events.title: A Friendly Under The Lights
events.body: A friendly under lights, with the shop open late and the terrace choir invited. The lights are older than the choir.

outcomes.successHeadline: Nine hundred people stay behind after the whistle
outcomes.text: The lights hold, the choir sings, and nine hundred people stay behind afterwards.
Half the lights fail at kickoff and the rest are not much better.

choices.label: Open the shop an hour early instead

outcomes.text: An extra hour, a decent queue, no risk taken.

events.title: The Car Park Argument
events.body: He is running their pressing drill and the squad is still arguing about it in the car park an hour later.

outcomes.successHeadline: The car park argument turns into how this club plays
outcomes.text: A fortnight later it is simply how this club plays, and nobody remembers arguing.
It does not survive contact with a Tuesday in November.
Half of it stays, half of it quietly disappears, nobody mentions it.

events.title: His First Club Feels Responsible
events.body: His first club knows the injury happened at their testimonial. Their chairman has phoned twice to say so.

choices.label: Let them pay for the specialist

outcomes.successHeadline: He is back a fortnight early and they refuse the invoice
outcomes.text: They pay for the specialist, refuse to be reimbursed, and he is back a fortnight early.
A second opinion, a third scan, and a longer wait than either club wanted.
Their physio drives over twice a week and will not take a fee.

events.title: All Forty Names
events.body: The work party would like their names on the wall. All forty of them. They have brought a list, alphabetised.

outcomes.successHeadline: Forty names in brass, and forty families who come to see them
outcomes.text: Forty names in brass, and forty families who turn up on the Saturday to find them.
Three names are misspelled. In brass. Permanently.
One line, well cast, screwed to the wall by the door.

events.title: He Would Like It In Writing
events.body: He has played every week since you gave him your word, and would like it in the contract rather than in June.

outcomes.successHeadline: He signs a year longer than his agent advised
outcomes.text: It goes in the contract and he signs a year longer than his agent advised.
He reads the clause properly and finds it says rather less than you did.
You say it again, out loud, and he takes you at your word again.

events.title: The Cutting In His Agent's Folder
events.body: He has not played. The local paper printed what you said, and his agent has kept the cutting.

outcomes.successHeadline: He plays like a man settling an argument
outcomes.text: He plays like a man settling an argument, and settles it.
He is not ready, and ninety minutes make that obvious to everybody.
You say plainly that you were wrong, which helps more than it should.

events.title: Three In One Afternoon
events.body: He took the match ball home. He has not put it down since, and the shop would quite like it back.

choices.label: Put him up for Player of the Month

outcomes.successHeadline: They read his name out at the ground
outcomes.text: He wins it, and they read his name out at the ground before kickoff.
He reads every word written about him and stops looking up.

choices.label: Frame it for the clubhouse wall

outcomes.text: The ball goes on the wall above the bar, signed by everybody who was there.

events.title: Six
events.body: The scoreboard operator turned it off with ten minutes left. Nobody asked him to turn it back on.

outcomes.successHeadline: They find four things and fix three of them
outcomes.text: Two hours in a cold room, four things found, three of them fixed by Thursday.
The video does what the result did, only slower and with the lights on.
Nothing is said until Monday, which is its own kind of message.

events.title: It Sold Out
events.body: The shop has sold out of something and the accountant would like you to know what. Four hundred mugs with the groundskeeper on them.

outcomes.successHeadline: He has started signing them
outcomes.text: The second batch goes in a fortnight and he has started signing them at the gate.
Four thousand mugs. The groundskeeper has stopped coming in.
Another four hundred mugs. They go in a fortnight as well.
